messages.subject: Part 3 error with count data and sleep diaries
parts:
Dear GGIR developers and community, 
I have been trying to use GGIR to process accelerometer data to detect sleep. We have count data and sleep diaries for all our participants and raw .bin files for a subset. Therefore to retain all our participants I would like to use the count data with sleep diaries rather than the .bin files. However, I seem to be running into an error message because i'm unable to set the def.noc.sleep to c() when there is a sleep diary and it forces a '1'. This subsequently seems to use the HASPT.algo="HDCZA". Furthermore, I am able to process the .bin file with sleep diaries with no errors. Is there a way to resolve this?
Here is my code:
GGIR(datadir = "Volumes/test/countdata",
     outputdir = "/Volumes/test/converted_output_withdiary",
     dataFormat="actiwatch_csv",
     extEpochData_timeformat="%d/%m/%Y%H:%M:%S",
     mode=1:5,
     do.report=c(2,4,5),
     idloc=2, #default is 1, but with idloc=2 GGIR looks at the filename and extracts the character string preceding the first occurance of a "_"
     windowsizes=c(30, 900,3600),#30istheexpectedepochlength
     visualreport=FALSE,
     outliers.only=FALSE,
     HASIB.algo="ColeKripke1992",
     HASPT.algo = "notused",
     #def.noc.sleep=c(),#<=becausewecannotuseHDCZAforZCY - don't need this when there is a sleep diary.
     sleepwindowType = "TimeInBed",
     relyonsleeplog = TRUE,
     #sleepeficiency.metric - default is 1, when it is 1 SE is detected sleep time divided by log sleep period, when it is 2 Se is detected sleep time devided by detected sleep period plus sleep latency (log sleep onset and accerlerometer sleep onset)
     sleepefficiency.metric = 2,
     #sleep diary information
     loglocation=("/Volumes/BMRI/CRU/HBA/HBA_Actigraphy/HBA GeneActiv Data/HBA actigraphy test/test/sleepdiary.csv"), #location of your sleep diary
     colid=1, #column the subject IDs are in
     coln1=2, #column where night 1 begins
     #excercise cut-offs
     threshold.lig = c(127.8),
     threshold.mod = c(187.6),  
     threshold.vig = c(396.4) #please cite: Dillion et al., 2016 if you use exercise: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC4858250/
)


Here is the error message:
Error message: 
______________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________
 Part 3
1 Error in quantile.default(x, probs = HDCZA_threshold[1]/100) :
  missing values and NaN's not allowed if 'na.rm' is FALSE
In addition: Warning messages:
1:
When dataFormat is set to actiwatch_csv we assume that metric is ZCY, this is now used
2:
When dataFormat is set to actiwatch_csv we assume that only metric ZCY is extracted and GGIR ignores all other metric requests. So, you should set arguments do.anglez & do.enmo to FALSE 



Here is what the count data looks like: 



Thank you all so much!

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Part 3 error with count data and sleep diaries
parts:
Hi Aaron,

You are specifying "extEpochData_timeformat="%d/%m/%Y%H:%M:%S","
but that is not how your data looks like. It has separate columns for date and time, which is not what GGIR expects. You will need to merge those columns and you probably are missing a space in the value of extEpochData_timeformat.

Best, Vincent

parts:
Dear Aaron,

An Actiwatch example file snippet that GGIR uses for testing can be found here: https://github.com/wadpac/GGIR/blob/master/inst/testfiles/Actiwatch.csv

It seems that this does not match the format you have created, which probably explains why GGIR cannot make sense of it.

Other facilitated data formats can be found here: https://github.com/wadpac/GGIR/tree/master/inst/testfiles

I would not be surprised if Actiwatch like most other accelerometer manufacturers generated many variations on their csv format being oblivious to the burden to research.

GGIR(datadir = datadir,
     outputdir = outputdir,
     mode = 1:5,
     overwrite = TRUE,
     windowsizes = c(60, 900, 3600),
     threshold.in = 1.5,
     threshold.mod = 3,
     threshold.vig = 6,
     dataFormat = "ami_csv",
     extEpochData_timeformat = "%m/%d/%Y %H:%M:%S",

     acc.metric = "ExtAct",
     desiredtz = "America/New_York",
     overwrite = TRUE,
     do.report = c(2, 4, 5),
     visualreport = FALSE)

For me this runs but I see that without access to sleep diary GGIR is not good yet at guessing the main resting period by which the sleep analyses is not informative. However, if that could be fixed then this may work.

parts:
Hi Aaron,

The documentation for HASPT.algo does not indicate that "notused" is an optional value. So, I do not understand why you expect this to work. GGIR expects a definition of the time window of being asleep, which we refer to as guider. A guider can be a sleeplog, HDCZA, HorAngle, etc. See documentation here for details.

"notused" is internally set when def.noc.sleep is specified as a vector of length two, being the assumed start and end time of the SPT or time in bed. So, this is one option if you do not have a sleeplog. However, in the Cookbook I indicated that setting HASPT.algo to c() is also an option, if you have no sleeplog. This looks for the least active 5 hours in the day and draws a 12 hour window around it. Whether either of these result into valid estimates of sleep is unknown, but at least those are the options currently implemented. Probably more research is needed to expand and improve the functionality. Funding and/or help for this is welcome.

Thanks,

Vincent

GGIR(datadir = datadir,
outputdir = outputdir,
mode = 1:5,
overwrite = TRUE,

extEpochData_timeformat = "%m/%d/%Y %H:%M:%S",
HASPT.algo = "NotWorn",
acc.metric = "ExtAct",
desiredtz = "America/New_York",
overwrite = TRUE,
do.report = c(2, 4, 5),
visualreport = FALSE)

For me this runs but I see that without access to sleep diary GGIR is not good yet at guessing the main resting period by which the sleep analyses is not informative. However, if that could be fixed then this may work.

Best, Vincent
